title: late-arrival-debouncer: timebound arbiter and soft-lease decay for continuous-batcher
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: Continuous-batcher suffers occasional tail spikes when small numbers of late-arriving requests repeatedly preempt in-flight coalesced batches or re-acquire hot KV cache pins, causing starvation of other lanes. This PR introduces a late-arrival debouncer and a timebound arbiter to smooth admission decisions and a soft-lease decay for slot leases to reduce repeated re-grabs. Goals: (1) reduce 95/99p tail latency under mixed arrival jitter without losing throughput, (2) avoid KV cache pin churn on micro-hot keys, (3) preserve fairness across priority lanes with a small bounded added latency for highly-jittered arrivals. Summary of changes: - scheduler/arbiter: add TimeboundArbiter which assigns a short, configurable admission window (debounce_window_ms) per batch slot; late arrivals that fall inside the window are coalesced rather than treated as fresh high-priority arrivals. - scheduler/leases: implement soft-lease-decay that reduces the effective priority of repeated immediate lease re-acquisitions by the same client for a short cooldown period, implemented as a probabilistic decay counter so behavior is smooth across scale. - kvcache: introduce shadow-pin accounting to detect churny keys; shadow pins don't block eviction immediately but track touch frequency to recommend prefetch/repin thresholds to the allocator. - batching heuristics: arrival-jitter-dampener which adds small, randomized jitter to waiting agents to avoid pathological synchrony. - metrics: new metrics (debounce.window_hits, soft_lease.decays, kv.shadow_pin_rate) and dashboards for per-queue hit/miss and fairness indices. - tests: added deterministic unit tests for debouncer logic and an integration benchmark harness that simulates mixed jitter workloads. Backwards compatibility and config: all features default to off/opt-in via runtime flags and rollout config; conservative defaults enabled for internal perf canaries. Perf results (canary): local perf lab with mixed microburst + jitter workload: 95p latency reduced by ~9% and 99p by ~14% on p50 routing; throughput unchanged within 0.5%. On a KV-heavy churn scenario (hot key fanout), observed ~30% reduction in shadow pin churn and a 7% reduction in token cost due to fewer cache repins. Checklist: - [x] Design doc + benchmark plan in ENG ticket ENG-7482 - [x] Unit + integration tests added - [x] Canary run against perf-lab - [x] Dashboard panels added - [x] Feature flag and rollout plan included Risk notes: soft-lease-decay may slightly increase latency for repeated short requests from same client; exposed via feature flag and gated behind rollout. Rollout plan: enable for internal canary pool -> expand to Dedicated regions with telemetry -> full rollout once fairness index stable for 48h. References: ENG-7482, ENG-7520, related PRs on queue fairness and lease reclaiming.

review_comments: Diego Ramos: Nice focused change. Concern: how does the TimeboundArbiter interact with existing lane preemption rules? Please add unit tests covering a high-priority request arriving mid-window.
Maya Patel (author): Added targeted unit test 'TestArbiter_PreemptDuringWindow' and documented preemption override rules in docs; arbiter yields to critical lanes if explicit override flag is set.
Anika Singh: The soft-lease-decay logic looks probabilistic; can we make the decay parameters observable (counters/histogram) so SRE can tune without code changes?
Maya Patel: Exposed counters soft_lease.decays and a decay_attempts histogram; added dashboard tile and instructions for tuning via rollout config.
Liam O'Connor: Integration test shows one flaky where debounce window boundary is off by 1ms on some runners. Can we tolerate +-2ms?
Maya Patel: Relaxed boundary checks in TestArbiter_TimingEdge and added jitter in test harness to avoid machine-clock artifacts. Verified in CI.

release_notes: Introduce TimeboundArbiter (late-arrival debouncing), soft-lease-decay to reduce repeated lease re-acquisitions, and shadow-pin tracking to mitigate KV cache churn. Config flags provided for staged rollout. Expected benefit: lower 95/99p latencies under arrival jitter and reduced KV repin costs.
notes: Feature gated behind 'late_arrival_debouncer' runtime flag. Dashboards added: Queue / Debounce window hits, Soft lease decays, KV shadow-pin churn. If regressions observed, disable flag and revert via cherry-pick hotfix branch.
testing_instructions: Run 'go test ./scheduler/... -run TestArbiter' and 'python3 internal/benchmarks/mixed_jitter_harness.py --mode canary' to reproduce bench scenarios. See docs/notes/late-arrival-debouncer.md for config knobs.
